fatal_errors: The proposed in situ TEM-EDS experiment does not reconstruct the study's comparison between as-printed and 750°C/50 h precipitation-aged SLM material.
The baseline is incorrectly defined as cast and wrought alloy rather than the as-printed, precipitate-free SLM state.
The temperature, gas-flow rate, ramp rate, and two-hour exposure are invented and conflict with the studied 600–1200°C, up-to-96-hour isothermal exposures.
The predicted 20% oxidation-rate reduction is unsupported and opposite to the observed higher mass gain of the aged material.
Weight gain per unit area cannot ordinarily be measured directly within an in situ TEM experiment as proposed.

The hypothesis omits the central mechanism: delayed formation of a continuous protective Cr2O3 scale due to Cr-depleted precipitates and short-circuit oxygen transport along precipitate–matrix interfaces.
explanation: TEM-EDS could, in principle, visualize nanoscale compositional redistribution, so the answer has limited relevance to the general question. However, the target mechanistic approach relied on comparative oxidation kinetics, cross-sectional SEM-EDS, XRD/Raman oxide identification, and initial-state neutron diffraction/SEM. The generated hypothesis invents unsupported conditions and quantitative thresholds, uses the wrong baseline, predicts the wrong trend, and does not identify the Cr2O3-mediated protection or the adverse role of Cr-depleted L12/L21 precipitates and their interfaces. Its falsification design also combines TEM with a bulk gravimetric measurement that the stated setup cannot directly provide.
